clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old female with history of pelvic radiotherapy for cervical cancer and bilateral ureteric strictures presented with severe haematuria and hemodynamic instability. Initial CT angiography showed the ureter inseparable from the iliac arteries but no active bleeding. Subsequent conventional catheter angiography demonstrated active bleeding from the right internal iliac artery into the distal ureter consistent with arterioureteral fistula. Diagnosis was confirmed by imaging showing contrast extravasation into the ureter and urinary bladder.
